Predict the Cumulative Incidence Function in One Step

Source: R/fine_gray_predict.R
predict_fine_gray.Rd

Fits a Fine-Gray model with [fine_gray()] and predicts the cumulative incidence function for `new_data` (or the training data) in one call.

Usage

predict_fine_gray(
  data,
  time_col,
  event_col,
  formula,
  new_data = NULL,
  times = NULL,
  failcode = 1,
  cencode = 0,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame, one row per subject.

time_col

Follow-up time.

event_col

Event type, as in [tbl_cumulative_incidence()]: a censoring code, then one code per cause.

formula

One-sided formula of the predictors, for example `~ age + arm`.

new_data

A data frame of new predictors. `NULL` (the default) predicts on `data`.

times

Times to predict the CIF at; `NULL` is every event time of the cause of interest in `data`.

failcode

Code of the cause of interest (default 1).

cencode

Code for censoring (default 0).

...

Passed to [fine_gray()] (and through it to `cmprsk::crr()`).

Value

As [predict.fine_gray_model()]: a tibble with one row per row of `new_data`, with a `.pred` list-column of `.eval_time` / `.pred_cif` tibbles.

See also

[fine_gray()], [predict.fine_gray_model()]

Examples

if (requireNamespace("cmprsk", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1)
  d <- data.frame(time = rexp(150, 0.1), type = sample(0:2, 150, TRUE, prob = c(0.3, 0.4, 0.3)),
                  age = rnorm(150, 60, 8), arm = rep(c("A", "B"), 75))
  predict_fine_gray(d, "time", "type", ~ age + arm, new_data = d[1:3, ], times = c(5, 10))
}
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   .pred           
#>   <list>          
#> 1 <tibble [2 × 2]>
#> 2 <tibble [2 × 2]>
#> 3 <tibble [2 × 2]>
